title: Electronic Systems Measurement and Troubleshooting
description: This course covers the measurement and characterization of electronic systems, data collection, and reporting results in industry-accepted formats. System and component performance are compared to published specifications and troubleshooting techniques are developed. Laboratory practice includes the proper use of standard test instruments.
outcomes:
Connect and configure a mixed-signal oscilloscope to measure complex analog and
digital signals
Identify and/or describe circuit and equipment elements and specifications that are relevant to performing accurate measurements.
Develop electrical wiring diagrams including electrical control panel layout, power distribution, loop drawings, and PLC I/O diagrams
Troubleshoot using electrical wiring diagram including power distribution and PLC I/O diagrams.
objectives: Measure DC and AC parameters of simple analog and digital electronic systems and components
Organize and present data in tabular and graphic formats using industry-standard software
Compare measured performance to published specifications and identify any performance deficiencies
Develop, present, and execute a logical troubleshooting plan appropriate for the subject system or component
Describe the function of field-effect, bipolar, and tyristor three-terminal devices in switching circuits
Memorize and demonstrate ohmmeter test techniques for common two- and three-terminal devices
Develop and present all electrical wiring diagrams including electrical control panel layout, power distribution, loop drawings, and PLC I/O diagrams
content: Microsoft Excel as a data collection and graphic presentation tool
Digital waveforms; logic levels and timing
Current/voltage characteristics of linear and non-linear two-terminal devices
Develop electrical wiring diagrams including electrical control panel layout, power distribution, loop drawings, and Programmable Logic Controller Input/Output (PLC I/O) diagrams
lab: Use Excel for data collection and graphic presentation
Measure Gain, bandwidth, decibels and etc.
Measure Digital waveforms; logic levels and timing
Distinguish Current/voltage characteristics of linear and non-linear two-terminal devices
Develop troubleshooting plan for faulty circuits
Using industry software to develop electrical wiring diagrams including electrical control panel layout, power distribution, loop drawings, and PLC I/O diagrams
assignments: Students are expected to work on homework in order to learn the materials
Example: List two common types of DMM displays, and discuss the advantages and disadvantages of each.
Students use the concepts and technical skills learned in the class to analyze and solve practical problems.
Example: From a specification sheet for a single-chip audio amplifier, identify the key performance parameters. Measure the
performance of a test unit, compile and present the results, and determine if the unit performance meets the specifications.
Example: Given a case study for a non-functioning electronic system, develop an initial troubleshooting plan to logically and effectively
isolate the fault. Example topic could be "Troubleshooting for Impact: Diagnosing Failure in a Low-Cost Pulse Oximeter"
